To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lactogenic receptors of rat liver, which have been previously characterized in terms of their molecular mass and subcellular distribution, are composed of two subunits, one of 63 kDa and the other of 30 kDa, and that the 130 kDa species, previously identified as a somatogenic receptor, is a complex of the lactogenic receptor and the cytoplasmic protein of 70 kD, which is a component of the endoplasmic reticulum.

the lactogenic and somatotropic receptors present in rat hepatocytes have been identified by means of cross-linking studies using a photoreactive derivative of hGH, and that the lactogenic receptors are associated with a protein of 63 kDa and a 45 kDa protein.
the lactogenic receptor of the rat liver is a 63 k Da species, which is present in the microsomal membrane and in the Triton X- 100-solubilized preparation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the demonstration of the presence of two distinct populations of lactogenic receptors in rat liver microsomal membranes.
the identification of the proteins associated with the somatogenic and the lactogenic receptors, in both intact hepatocytes and microsomal preparations.

the identification of proteins associated with the lactogenic and somatotropine receptors, and with the demonstration that the 130 kDa protein is related to the binding sites for somatotropins, and the 63 kDa protein to those for prolactin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 70 kDa species is related to the lactogenic binding sites, the 63 kDa to both lactogenic and somatotropinic binding sites and the 45 kDa to somatotropine binding sites.
lactogenic and somatotropic binding sites present in microsomal membrane preparations and hepatocytes, have a different molecular weight, and are associated with different protein species.
the lactogenic receptors of rat hepatocytes are present as a single polypeptide of 63 kDa, whereas the somatogenic receptors are present as a 130 kDa polypeptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AP-hGH1 is a suitable probe to study the lactogenic receptors in both microsomal membranes, Triton X- 100-solubilized membranes, and intact hepatocytes, whereas it is a useful tool to investigate the somatogenic receptors in the latter.
the lactogenic and somatotropic receptors present in rat hepatocytes are related to a 63 and 73 kDa species respectively.
the somatogenic and the lactogenic receptors are present as monomeric species in the microsomal membranes, and as a dimer and a tetramer in the hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

lactogenic receptors in liver microsomal membranes are composed of a polypeptide of 63 kDa, while somatogenic receptors are composed of a 130 kDa polypeptide and at least three additional polypeptides of 70-73 kDa, 63 kDa and 45 kDa.
the lactogenic receptors in rat liver are associated with a 63 kda protein, which may be a proteolytic product of a larger protein, since it is present in microsomal preparations as well.
AP-hGH1 has a similar specificity to that of the unmodified hGH.
